title: Signalized prefetch experiment summary for long-context MoE + dense models
content:
Summary:
This doc collects the results and informal interpretation of the "signalized prefetch" experiments run across Llama-13B, Mistral-7B, Qwen-14B and a Qwen-MoE prototype. The goal: reduce p95 tail latency for long-context (8k-32k token windows) generation workloads while keeping unit cost close to baseline. Signalized prefetch = use lightweight per-request signals (session type, prompt entropy, recent KV-access density) to decide adaptive prefetch window sizes and whether to warm expert shards.

What we ran (short):
- Workloads: synthetic long-form generation + two customer conversation traces (support-chat, doc-summarization). Context lengths: 8k, 16k, 32k.
- Models: Llama-13B (dense), Mistral-7B (dense, different layernorm placement), Qwen-14B (dense, chunked attention optimizations), Qwen-MoE-proto (same base + MoE layers 2/4/6 gating).
- Infra: 8x A100-80GB per node tests, CUDA 12.3, runtime build v2024.10. Nsight system captures + per-token tracing (microtrace).

Key numeric highlights (median of 5 runs, mixed batch sizes):
- Baseline p95 (32k): Llama: 1.9s/token; Mistral: 2.6s/token; Qwen: 1.5s/token; Qwen-MoE: 3.8s/token (gating jitter).
- With signalized prefetch (signal threshold tuned on entropy + kv-density): p95 improves: Llama -25% (1.43s), Mistral -18% (2.13s), Qwen -10% (1.35s), Qwen-MoE -32% (2.6s).
- KV cache hit-rate effect: prefetch window of 64 tokens increased effective KV hit-rate by ~12% on doc-summarization traces; but for support-chat (lots of small context switches) hit-rate decrease observed without session affinity.
- Throughput (tokens/sec) saw small regressions (2-6%) due to extra prefetch ops, compensated by fewer long tail spikes.

Observations / Architecture-specific behaviors: 
- Llama-13B (dense): prefetching helps because dense attention kernels are compute-bound and warming KV + preallocating attention scratch reduces kernel launch stalls. Kernel heatmaps show reduced stalled time in attention_fwd after prefetch.
- Mistral-7B: layernorm placement + fused FFN makes per-layer memory jitter higher. Prefetch reduces end-to-end tail but less effective than on Llama because memory reclamation in our allocator happens mid-forward and sometimes cancels prefetch gains. A follow-up allocator tweak (eager-scratch-reserve) shows promise.
- Qwen-14B: already benefits from chunked attention; signalized prefetch only marginally helps p50 but reduces p95 moderately. Chunked attention & streaming KV layout are the reason — prefetch should prefer larger chunk alignment to avoid partial-chunk loads.
- Qwen-MoE prototype: gating variability dominates tail. Two effects: (1) expert hot-spoting leads to serialization (some experts receive many routed tokens, creating a local queue), (2) gating compute (softmax over experts + top-k selection) has variance tied to input token distribution. Prefetching that warms expert embeddings reduces remote fetch cost but does not eliminate gating jitter. We saw a remaining p95 gap from dense models even after prefetch.

Profiling nuggets (tools + traces):
- Use Nsight line-based traces to correlate timeline with per-kernel occupancy. Microtrace token-level logs useful to find timestamp gaps between kv_update and attention kernels.
- Heavy tail correlates with: non-empty GPU-to-GPU memcpy (shuffle of expert shards), host-side gating compute blocking before kernel dispatch, and kernel launch spikes when prefetched buffers require allocation.
- Kernel names to watch: attention_fwd, attention_bwd (if training), dense_mm, kv_update_copy, gating_compute, expert_apply, alloc_scratch.

Root-cause hypotheses we validated: 
1) Gating jitter + expert hot-spoting (MoE) -> tail: mitigated partially by warming expert state and smoothing gating decisions (moving-average of gate logits). Warm-up reduces memcpy spikes but cannot fix queuing when an expert receives >3x average token fanout.
2) Fragmented prefetch windows increase allocator churn -> tail: solved by large-alignment prefetch and keeping a per-thread scratch pool.
3) Cross-model kernel fit: Mistral's fused ops amplify allocator/caching inefficiencies -> tail: minor runtime changes (eager-scratch-reserve + pinned scratch) drop p95 by ~12% on Mistral.

Micro-experiments we ran (notes):
- Prefetch thresholds: entropy-only vs kv-density-only vs combined. Combined signal wins across traces; entropy-only misfires on templated prompts.
- Warm-expert-only for MoE vs full buffer prefetch: warm-expert-only gives 60% of the benefit at 30% of the extra memory cost. Good trade-off for most production scenarios.
- Gate-smoothing: apply exponent decay smoothing to gate logits over last N tokens -> reduces gating volatility but introduces slight quality diff in expert selection. Need eval run.

Actionable mitigations (short term):
- Ship signalized prefetch as opt-in per model route; default conservative thresholds.
- Add per-worker pinned scratch pool and large-alignment prefetch allocation to avoid allocator stalls. (PR referenced in linked_artifacts)
- For MoE-heavy customers: add warm-expert-only mode and gating-smoothing flag as runtime knobs.
- Instrument per-request signal (kv-density + entropy) in tracing pipeline so we can correlate decisions to tail events in prod.

Longer term / research ideas: 
- Adaptive routing at runtime: if an expert becomes hot, proactively re-balance by temporary duplicate expert inflight (replica routing) — simulation stage only.
- Combine prefetch with model-aware kernel fusion for Mistral: try fusing kv_update + attention_fwd to remove launch gap.
- Explore scheduler level backpressure where requests with high prefetch cost are deprioritized to protect SLOs.

Open questions / risks:
- Quality impact of gate-smoothing and warm-expert heuristics on downstream generation quality needs offline eval (we have relevant eval buckets but not complete).
- Memory cost of prefetch at 32k contexts for large batch mixes can exceed node headroom; need better admission control.

Next steps / owners: 
- Mateo: land per-worker pinned scratch pool (PR #482) and run Mistral allocator sweep (dued 2024-11-12).
- Alex: run quality eval for gate-smoothing on customer traces and report delta (dued 2024-11-14).
- Hana: instrument per-request signals in tracing pipeline and add dashboards for prefetch decisions (dued 2024-11-20).
- Priya: consolidate longer-run scheduling experiments and simulation for replica routing (dued 2024-12-05).

Notes to self: keep experiment traces (nsys captures) archived under s3://redwood-experiments/signalized-prefetch/; include sample microtrace ids in jira SERV-9342.

Appendix (raw numbers/plots available in linked PR):
- Full CSV of runs attached to PR 482 (tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, memory footprint).
- Quick cheat: if p95 > 3x p50 and gating_compute occupies >20% of timeline -> suspect MoE gating jitter.

End of summary.
